resources.name: REA

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: OpenContext

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Trail-code
resources.description: A local map of a codebase plus team learnings, so coding agents go to the right files and pick up earlier decisions.

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

Mods run with your account's permissions; review them before installing. MIT.

resources.name: jCodeMunch MCP

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: CodeGraph

resources.description: Stripe's API for payments, subscriptions, invoices and the events behind them.
resources.for_whom: Agents and apps that read or manage billing.
resources.access_notes: Use a restricted API key with only the permissions the job needs, and test in a sandbox before using live keys. A restricted key for an autonomous agent can be tagged as an agent key; agent-tagged keys need a designated reviewer to approve sensitive actions, and from December 2026 Stripe's MCP server stops accepting full-access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag. The published limits are 100 requests a second in live mode and 25 in a sandbox, with a 25-a-second limit on most endpoints and further exceptions. Read requests must also average no more than 500 per transaction over a rolling 30 days, with a minimum allowance of 10,000 a month. A key that can read invoices shouldn't be able to refund or pay out, so scope it accordingly.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Resend API
resources.description: An email API for transactional and marketing email, with inbound handling.
resources.for_whom: Agents and apps that send email from a verified domain.
resources.access_notes: Authenticate with an API key that can be limited by permission and domain. The free plan covers 3,000 emails a month, up to 100 a day. The default API limit is 10 requests a second per team, separate from sending quotas. Recipients' details and email content are customer data, and API access doesn't give consent to email anyone.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Notion API
resources.description: Notion's API for pages, databases, comments and files in a workspace.
resources.for_whom: Agents that read or update a team's Notion workspace.
resources.access_notes: Connect with an internal connection token, a personal access token or OAuth; each reaches only the pages shared with it. A personal token acts as its user. Limits are 600 requests a minute per connection on Business and Enterprise plans and 180 on other plans, plus workspace limits, so honour Retry-After. Querying a data source has its own limit of about 3 requests a second per connection.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: HeyGen API
resources.description: HeyGen's API for avatar video, images, voice and translation.
resources.for_whom: Teams producing video with AI avatars or translated voice.
resources.access_notes: The API uses an API key with scopes and bills against an API plan. The MCP server and CLI sign in as your web account and use its subscription credits instead, so a web plan isn't API credit. Limits vary by endpoint and plan. Using a person's likeness or voice needs their consent.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: NVIDIA NIM API catalog
resources.description: Hosted model endpoints from NVIDIA for prototyping, with some models also available to run yourself.
resources.for_whom: Developers trying open models before choosing where to run them.
resources.access_notes: Needs an NVIDIA developer account and API key. Developer Program access is for prototyping, research, development and testing only; production, which NVIDIA defines to include anything serving real end users, needs an NVIDIA AI Enterprise licence. The API trial terms bar confidential information and, unless a service allows it, personal data, and say NVIDIA sets use limits; the docs give no rate limit figure. The model list at https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/models answers without a key, and a retired model's id returns HTTP 410 with its end-of-life date. Each model's licence and terms apply separately.
resources.verification: Official documentation and API trial terms reviewed; keyless model list queried

resources.name: GitHub REST API
resources.description: GitHub's API for repositories, issues, pull requests, releases and users.
resources.for_whom: Agents that read or manage code and project work on GitHub.
resources.access_notes: Use a fine-grained personal access token, a GitHub App or OAuth; workflows get a built-in token. Unauthenticated calls to public endpoints allow 60 an hour, and an authenticated user gets 5,000 an hour, with separate limits for search and apps. A public repository still has its own licence, so check it before reusing code.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Supabase APIs
resources.description: The Supabase Management API for projects, alongside each project's own database, auth and storage APIs.
resources.for_whom: Agents that set up or manage Supabase projects.
resources.access_notes: The Management API uses a scoped personal access token or OAuth. Each project's data APIs use their own keys and row-level security, which is a separate layer. The free plan covers two active projects, and inactive ones pause. Never expose a management or service key in a client app.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Influencers Club MCP server
resources.description: Search creators on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and other platforms from an MCP client, with profile, audience and lookalike data.
resources.for_whom: Marketers looking for creators whose audience matches their buyers.
resources.access_notes: Needs an Influencers Club account with API credits, and each call spends them. A local install reads an API key from the environment, and its batch tools read and write local files. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: vidIQ MCP server
resources.description: Gives an AI client vidIQ's YouTube data: video and channel stats, outlier videos, keyword research, comments, transcripts and earnings estimates.
resources.for_whom: Marketers and creators researching YouTube channels and content.
resources.access_notes: Needs a vidIQ account, and hosted tools may use credits. It reads data for the channels you authorise, and some tools can make approved edits to videos you own. Apache 2.0 licence for the plugin.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: YouTube Data API
resources.description: Google's official API for public channel, video and playlist data, such as subscriber, view and comment counts.
resources.for_whom: Developers building channel analysis into agents.
resources.access_notes: Needs a Google Cloud project and an API key. The default quota is 10,000 units a day, and most reads cost 1 unit. Changes to a channel need its owner's OAuth consent.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: yt-dlp
resources.description: A command line tool that downloads video, audio, subtitles and metadata from YouTube and many other sites.
resources.for_whom: Agents and people who need a video's files or metadata on their own machine.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account. Downloads must respect each site's terms and copyright. Unlicense.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: youtube-transcript-api
resources.description: A Python library that fetches a YouTube video's transcript or subtitles, including auto-generated ones, without an API key.
resources.for_whom: Developers who need video text for analysis or summaries.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account or key. It reads YouTube's caption data, which can change or be rate limited. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Social Blade
resources.description: Public statistics, growth history and estimated earnings for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Twitch accounts.
resources.for_whom: Anyone sizing a creator's reach and growth from public data.
resources.access_notes: Public pages are free to read. Reports and an API are for business customers. Earnings figures are estimates from public view counts.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: YouTube Analytics API
resources.description: Google's official API for targeted queries on a channel's own analytics, such as views, ratings, audience age, gender and country, and estimated revenue.
resources.for_whom: Channel owners, agencies and the agents they authorise to report on a channel's performance.
resources.access_notes: Needs OAuth consent from the channel or content owner, so it cannot read another creator's private analytics unless they grant access. The yt-analytics.readonly scope covers activity metrics, revenue needs the separate yt-analytics-monetary.readonly scope, and Google sets a quota cost for each query. The YouTube API Services Terms and Developer Policies apply, including limits on storing data and on combining data from different content owners.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: YouTube Reporting API
resources.description: Google's official API for scheduled bulk reports of a channel's or content owner's analytics, delivered as daily CSV files.
resources.for_whom: Analysts who want a channel's full daily history in their own database.
resources.access_notes: Needs OAuth consent from the channel or content owner, with the same read-only and monetary scopes as the Analytics API. A new reporting job backfills 30 days, the first files can take 48 hours, and reports stay downloadable for 60 days, or 30 days for backfilled history. The YouTube API Services Terms and Developer Policies limit how long stored data can be kept without a refresh.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: youtube-comment-downloader
resources.description: A Python command line tool and library that downloads a YouTube video's comments to JSON or CSV without the YouTube API.
resources.for_whom: Analysts reading audience reaction on specific videos.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account or API key and writes comments, including commenter names, to a local file. It reads YouTube's web pages rather than the official API, and YouTube's Terms of Service bar automated access without YouTube's written permission. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: NewPipe Extractor
resources.description: The Java library behind the NewPipe app that reads YouTube videos, channels, comments, playlists, search and trending lists, and also supports SoundCloud, PeerTube and Bandcamp.
resources.for_whom: Java and Android developers who want YouTube data without the official API.
resources.access_notes: Runs inside your app with no account or API key, added as a dependency from JitPack or Maven Central. It scrapes YouTube's pages, which YouTube's Terms of Service bar without permission, and changes on YouTube's side can break it. GPL-3.0 licence, so software that ships it must meet the GPL's terms.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: pytubefix
resources.description: A Python library that reads YouTube video details, captions, channels, playlists and search results, and downloads streams.
resources.for_whom: Python developers who need captions or a channel's video list without an API key.

It reads YouTube's web player rather than the official API, YouTube's Terms of Service bar automated access and downloads without permission, and changes on YouTube's side can break it. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: YouTube.js
resources.description: A JavaScript client for YouTube's internal InnerTube API that reads video details, channels, comments, playlists and search results.
resources.for_whom: Node.js, Deno and browser developers building YouTube research into agents.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no API key; it caches session data by default and can use your account cookies for signed-in requests, which gives it that account's access. InnerTube is undocumented and YouTube's Terms of Service bar automated access without permission, so expect breakage and check your use. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Whisper
resources.description: OpenAI's open speech recognition model and command line tool, which transcribes audio in many languages and can translate it into English.
resources.for_whom: People who need a transcript for a video that has no captions.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account; it needs Python, PyTorch and ffmpeg, downloads model weights on first use, and models need from about 1 GB to about 10 GB of GPU memory. You need the right to download and transcribe the audio you give it. MIT licence for the code and model weights.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: faster-whisper
resources.description: A reimplementation of Whisper on the CTranslate2 inference engine, with 8-bit quantisation on CPU and GPU.
resources.for_whom: Developers running Whisper transcription in their own pipelines.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account and downloads converted models from the Hugging Face Hub on first use. It decodes audio with PyAV, so a system ffmpeg is not needed, while GPU use needs NVIDIA's CUDA libraries. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: whisper.cpp
resources.description: A C and C++ port of Whisper that runs on CPUs, Apple Silicon and a range of GPUs, with a command line tool and bindings for other languages.
resources.for_whom: People transcribing on a Mac or on a machine without a large GPU.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account; you build it from source and download ggml model files with the included script. The command line tool reads only 16-bit WAV files, so convert other audio with ffmpeg first. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: WhisperX
resources.description: A transcription tool built on faster-whisper that adds word-level timestamps and speaker labels.
resources.for_whom: Analysts transcribing interviews, podcasts or panel videos where who said what matters.
resources.access_notes: Runs locally with no account for transcription, and GPU use needs NVIDIA's CUDA toolkit. Speaker labels need a Hugging Face read token and acceptance of the user agreement for the pyannote speaker-diarization-community-1 model, and alignment models are downloaded per language. BSD-2-Clause licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: yutu
resources.description: A CLI, MCP server and agent mode that work through the official YouTube Data API, with optional Analytics and Reporting API access.
resources.for_whom: Channel teams who want an agent to read and manage their own YouTube channel.
resources.access_notes: Needs your own Google Cloud project and OAuth client, and it saves client_secret.json and youtube.token.json in the working folder unless you set its environment variables. The OAuth grant lets it create, update and delete videos, playlists and comments on that channel, and agent mode sends prompts to the Gemini or OpenAI key you supply. Data API quota applies; Apache 2.0 licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: YouTube MCP Server (ZubeidHendricks)
resources.description: An MCP server with read-only tools for YouTube video, channel, playlist and transcript lookups, plus creator search filtered by subscriber count and recent uploads.
resources.for_whom: Marketers using an MCP client to shortlist creators by size and activity.
resources.access_notes: Needs a YouTube Data API key in the environment, and each search spends that key's daily quota. It can fall back to a second and third key when one runs out, but the YouTube API Services Terms forbid getting round quota limits, so configure one key. Channel results can include emails found in public metadata, which are personal information; MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: YouTube Transcript MCP server
resources.description: An MCP server that fetches a YouTube video's captions, with optional timestamps, and by default strips sponsor and promotional sections marked by chapters.
resources.for_whom: People who want an agent to read or summarise what a video says.
resources.access_notes: Runs through npx with no account or key for transcripts. It reads YouTube's caption data outside the official API, which YouTube's Terms of Service restrict, and the optional video analysis tool sends a direct video URL to TwelveLabs under your own TwelveLabs key. MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Supadata
resources.description: An API and MCP server for transcripts and metadata from YouTube and other video platforms, with AI-generated transcripts billed by the minute.
resources.for_whom: Developers who want transcripts through a paid API instead of running their own scraper.
resources.access_notes: Needs a Supadata account and API key, or OAuth sign-in for the hosted MCP server at api.supadata.ai/mcp; the local server reads SUPADATA_API_KEY. The free plan gives 100 credits a month at one request a second, a transcript costs 1 credit, and a generated transcript costs 2 credits a minute. The MCP server code is MIT licensed.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: HypeAuditor MCP server
resources.description: HypeAuditor's hosted MCP server for YouTube, Instagram and TikTok creator analytics, including subscriber demographics, authenticity scores, growth and price estimates.
resources.for_whom: Brands and agencies vetting creators before paying for a campaign.
resources.access_notes: Sign in with a HypeAuditor Pro or higher account; creator analytics spend AI credits at US$0.005 each, about 10 for a search and 100 for an analysed account, and the assistant asks before any paid unlock. It can also create media plans and move creators between campaigns in your account. HypeAuditor's terms bar bots and scraping outside its API, which is a separate product sold through its sales team.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Arcmira
resources.description: A hosted transcript search service and MCP server for YouTube and podcasts that finds quotes, mentions, media appearances, ad reads and recurring channel sponsors.
resources.for_whom: Researchers tracking what is said about a brand and which brands sponsor which channels.
resources.access_notes: Sign in through your MCP client or use an arc_sk_ account key; the free plan has 1,000 credits a month and withholds the newest 30 days, and sponsor and ad-read data needs the Pro+ plan. Reads cost credits per row, and the write tool can create and pause monitors but not delete them. Speaker and sponsor labels can be incomplete, and the MCP server's repository, arcmira/mcp, has a proprietary licence that only permits running the published server; the Claude Code plugin and its skills, in its plugins/arcmira folder, are Apache-2.0.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: 1of10 MCP
resources.description: Connects Claude or ChatGPT to 1of10's database of YouTube outlier videos, which beat their channel's usual views, and to its title and thumbnail tracking.
resources.for_whom: Creators and strategists looking for video ideas that already work in a niche.
resources.access_notes: Needs a 1of10 Pro (US$89 a month) or Ultra plan, and you connect by signing in from its Claude and ChatGPT page; the server link for other clients appears only after sign-in. Research does not use credits but generating titles, ideas or thumbnails does, and it can save videos, create trackers and link your channel without deleting anything. There is no public API reference beyond the product page.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: SponsorBlock API
resources.description: The public API and database behind SponsorBlock, with crowdsourced timestamps for sponsor reads, self-promotion, intros and other segments in YouTube videos.
resources.for_whom: Analysts measuring how often and how long channels run sponsor segments.

The API and database are under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 unless the maintainer gives permission, so commercial use needs that permission and reuse needs attribution. Automated submissions are not allowed, and segments are community votes rather than verified facts.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Return YouTube Dislike API
resources.description: A public API that returns like counts and estimated dislike counts for YouTube videos, built from archived dislike data and estimates extrapolated from its extension's users.

resources.access_notes: No account or key is needed, and each client is limited to 100 requests a minute and 10,000 a day. Third-party use must credit the project with a link to its repository or returnyoutubedislike.com. Dislike figures for the period since YouTube hid them are estimates, so label them as such.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: SerpApi YouTube Search API
resources.description: A paid API that returns YouTube search results as JSON, including videos, channels, Shorts, view counts and subscriber counts.

Cached searches are free, and an output option returns Markdown for agents. SerpApi's U.S. Legal Shield, its cover for scraping and parsing search data, starts on the Production plan.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: NoxInfluencer API
resources.description: NoxInfluencer's API for YouTube, TikTok and Instagram creator profiles, videos, comments, search and contact details.
resources.for_whom: Agencies building creator search or vetting into their own tools.
resources.access_notes: A free trial gives 80 one-time credits, and ongoing access uses a Nox Key set up through an account manager with quoted pricing; each key is limited to 60 requests a minute. The site's terms forbid crawling NoxInfluencer data, so use the API rather than automating the web app. Contact details it returns are personal information.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Modash API
resources.description: Modash's Discovery and Raw APIs for searching and analysing YouTube, Instagram and TikTok creators, with audience demographics, lookalikes, audience overlap and recent posts.

Modash also offers an MCP server for the same data. The API terms bar standalone resale of raw results and require a lawful basis for processing creator data.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Phyllo
resources.description: A social data API that returns creators' public data and, with each creator's sign-in and consent, private data such as audience demographics and income from supported platforms, including YouTube.
resources.for_whom: Agencies and creator platforms that need data a creator has agreed to share.

resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: ChannelCrawler
resources.description: A YouTube channel database whose API searches over 35 million channels by niche, location, size and engagement and returns video lists and subscriber history, with sponsorship tracking in the web app.
resources.for_whom: Brands and agencies finding channels to sponsor and checking which creators competitors sponsor.
resources.access_notes: The API uses a bearer key and prepaid credits, from 100 credits for US$24, charged per result, with free search previews and email lookups billed only when an email is found. Sponsorship tracking is part of the web app's Power and Enterprise plans, not the API. Business emails it returns are personal information, so outreach must follow spam and privacy law.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Apify YouTube Scraper
resources.description: An Apify actor that collects public YouTube video and channel data, such as titles, views, likes, subscriber counts and upload dates, with optional subtitles.

The free plan's US$5 monthly credit covers a small run. It scrapes YouTube outside the official API, which YouTube's Terms of Service bar without permission, and Apify says not to collect personal data without a legitimate reason.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: ThoughtLeaders CLI
resources.description: A command line client for ThoughtLeaders' YouTube sponsorship data, covering which brands sponsor which channels, lookalike channels, transcripts, view curves and audience profiles.
resources.for_whom: Brand and agency teams using an agent to research sponsorship history before a pitch.
resources.access_notes: Needs a ThoughtLeaders account, signed in by browser OAuth, device code or API key, and every query spends credits, with recommender tools on the Intelligence plan at 25 credits a call. It can add comments to records, signing out ends every session, and tl setup writes skill files into your agent's folders. Needs Python 3.12 or later with jq, ripgrep, duckdb and yt-dlp; MIT licence.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Paseo
resources.description: A desktop, mobile, web and CLI app that runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode and other coding agents side by side, each in its own worktree.
resources.for_whom: People who want to run and steer several coding agent CLIs from one desktop app and their phone.
resources.access_notes: Download the desktop app from paseo.sh/download or GitHub Releases, or on a server run npm install -g @getpaseo/cli then paseo. Needs at least one agent CLI already signed in; Paseo uses that login and stores no provider keys. The daemon listens on 127.0.0.1:6767 with no password by default, so anything that can reach that port can control your agents. Set one with paseo daemon set-password before exposing it, or pair a phone through the end-to-end encrypted relay. New Claude agents default to Auto mode, where a model classifier answers permission prompts (Always Ask on Bedrock or Vertex). Plugins run with access to the daemon machine. The README says there is no telemetry. The LICENSE file grants Apache-2.0 for Paseo and leaves third-party components under their own licences; GitHub shows NOASSERTION.
resources.verification: Official documentation and licence reviewed; not installed or independently tested

resources.name: Happy
resources.description: A desktop and phone app that runs Claude, Codex, Grok and other coding agents on your own machine, with end-to-end encrypted sync and sessions you can share.
resources.for_whom: People who want to use the Claude, Codex or Grok subscriptions they already pay for and follow or steer the agent from a phone or with a colleague.
resources.access_notes: Desktop app from happy.engineering; phone apps on the App Store and Google Play. The original CLI is npm install -g happy, then happy claude or happy codex, which shows a QR code to pair a phone. Agents sign in with your own Claude, Codex and Grok subscriptions. Sessions sync end-to-end encrypted through Happy's server (api.cluster-fluster.com by default); message IDs, timestamps and device IDs are not encrypted. npm install -g happy-server-self-host then happy server runs your own sync server. The app sends PostHog usage analytics until you turn them off in Settings. Optional voice sends microphone audio and session context to ElevenLabs outside the encryption. Anyone you invite into a session can steer its agent. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation and licence reviewed; not installed or independently tested

resources.name: Claude Squad
resources.description: A terminal app that manages several Claude Code, Codex, Gemini or Aider sessions at once, each in its own tmux session and git worktree.
resources.for_whom: Developers who want parallel coding agents on one repository from a single terminal window.
resources.access_notes: brew install claude-squad, or curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smtg-ai/claude-squad/main/install.sh | bash, which puts cs in ~/.local/bin. Read the script before running it. Needs tmux and the GitHub CLI (gh). The default program is claude; start others with cs -p "codex", and the README sets OPENAI_API_KEY for Codex. The s key commits and pushes the session's branch to GitHub. The experimental -y (--autoyes) flag accepts every prompt for Claude Code and Aider without asking. Config is in ~/.claude-squad/config.json. AGPL-3.0.
resources.verification: Official documentation and licence reviewed; not installed or independently tested

resources.name: audio.cpp
resources.description: A C++ inference engine built on ggml that runs local audio models for speech synthesis and recognition, voice cloning and conversion, voice activity detection and music.
resources.for_whom: Developers running speech, voice or music models on their own Windows, Linux or Mac machine from a CLI, server or web UI.
resources.access_notes: Prebuilt binaries for Windows, Ubuntu and macOS are on GitHub Releases. On macOS, brew tap 0xShug0/audio-cpp, brew trust 0xShug0/audio-cpp, then brew install audio-cpp. Or build from source with CMake. Runs locally with no account. Model packages download from Hugging Face or ModelScope, and Hugging Face requests can carry your HF_TOKEN. audiocpp_server --ui --ui-management serves a web UI at http://127.0.0.1:8080 that can download models and take uploads. Model weights keep their own licences and some bar commercial use; docs/model_licenses.md lists them. The LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 (copyright ShugoAI LLC); GitHub shows NOASSERTION.
resources.verification: Official documentation and licence reviewed; not installed or independently tested

resources.name: Floci
resources.description: A local AWS emulator for development, tests and CI that serves AWS-shaped services at localhost:4566 and can replace LocalStack Community.
resources.for_whom: Developers who test AWS SDK, CLI, Terraform or CDK code on their machine or in CI without an AWS account.
resources.access_notes: docker compose up with the floci/floci image on port 4566, or floci start with the Floci CLI; a standalone binary is on GitHub Releases. Needs no AWS account or auth token, and any non-empty credentials work unless you turn on service auth checks. Lambda, RDS, ECS, EC2, EKS and other services run real containers and need the Docker socket mounted, which gives Floci control of Docker on the host. The web console at localhost:4566/_floci/ui starts a sidecar on port 4500, published on every interface unless you set FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_BIND_ADDRESS. Data stays in memory by default. MIT.
resources.verification: Official documentation and licence reviewed; not installed or independently tested

resources.name: Are you found by AI? DNS-AID checker
resources.description: Check a domain's DNS-AID index record against DNS-AID draft-02, an IETF Internet-Draft that is still a work in progress. It checks DNS only, and a DNS-AID record does not change your Are you found by AI? score. It looks for an SVCB record (type 64) at _index._agents.yourdomain.com and does not test the endpoint the record points to, its TLS connection or whether an AI engine uses it.
resources.for_whom: People who operate an agent index and want to see whether their domain publishes its DNS-AID record.
resources.access_notes: Free web form that asks only for a domain, with no sign-in. The page sends that domain to areyoufoundbyai.com, which looks up the record and shows the queried name, the target and whether the resolver reports an authenticated answer. The page says no DNS-AID setup is needed unless you operate an agent index, and to read its setup requirements at areyoufoundbyai.com/guides/dns-aid before changing DNS.
resources.verification: Official documentation reviewed; not independently tested

resources.name: Playwright MCP
resources.description: Microsoft's MCP server that lets an agent drive a real browser with Playwright, reading each page as an accessibility snapshot so it needs no screenshots or vision model.
resources.for_whom: Developers who want an agent to browse sites, fill in forms or test a web app from Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, Cursor or another MCP client.

resources.for_whom: DeepSeek Harness users who want several persistent agents to share work in group chats, on their own computer, a NAS or another always-on machine.
resources.access_notes: Download the desktop app from GitHub Releases for Windows, macOS or Linux (it bundles DSH), add the ds-bot plugin in DSH Desktop, or for DSH Web run npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1 plugin --profile web add ds-bot then npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1 web, which needs Node.js 22.19 or later and pnpm. A Docker image suits a NAS or server; bots get full access to whatever you mount into the container. You need a DeepSeek account or API key, and DeepSeek bills by usage; group chats cost more, and coding-agent CLIs such as Claude Code or Codex can run a bot on their own sign-in and plan. Bot data stays in bot/ and sessions/ under ~/.dsh and is not deleted when you uninstall the plugin, but bots use your model quota, and the default auto web search falls back to the public result pages of Bing and DuckDuckGo. The Windows installer is not signed yet, so check its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt; the Windows app and Linux AppImage update themselves. The main bot has very high rights over other bots and group chats, and bots read and write files and run commands when asked. A local MCP command a bot adds needs your approval, emails wait for you to send them by default, and computer use is set per bot with a level and an app list. This is a community project, not an official DeepSeek product. Apache-2.0.

resources.name: SkillSpector
resources.description: A scanner from NVIDIA that checks AI agent skills and MCP servers for prompt injection, data exfiltration, supply-chain and other risks before you install them, and gives each a risk score from 0 to 100.
resources.for_whom: Developers and security teams who install third-party skills into Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or similar agents and want to know whether a skill is safe first.
resources.access_notes: Install with uv tool install git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git, or with uv tool install 'skillspector[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector.git' to also run it as an MCP server (claude mcp add skillspector -- skillspector mcp). A Dockerfile is included if you would rather not install Python. Needs Python 3.12 to 3.15. LLM analysis is on by default and sends the scanned files' contents to the configured provider, which defaults to NVIDIA's build.nvidia.com with an NVIDIA_INFERENCE_KEY; OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, local Ollama and the Claude, Gemini and OpenCode CLIs also work, and --no-llm keeps file contents local. The dependency check sends package names and versions to OSV.dev even with --no-llm. The MCP HTTP transport has no authentication and only binds to loopback addresses, and the README notes a known initialise hang on the stdio transport (issue #199). It never runs the scanned skill and does not sandbox a skill you install anyway. Apache-2.0.

resources.name: NVIDIA Auto Ontology
resources.description: An open library from NVIDIA that builds an ontology from database metadata and serves it to agents through MCP, CLI and API, so they answer data questions with SQL that is checked against the database.
resources.for_whom: Data and platform teams who want agents to answer analytics questions over SQL sources such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake and Databricks using shared, certified definitions.
resources.access_notes: Runs as a self-hosted stack: clone the repo, copy .env.example to .env, then docker compose up -d --build; a Helm chart covers Kubernetes. Requires Docker with Compose v2, uv and an NVIDIA API key (nvapi-...) from build.nvidia.com, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint set per model role. By default the models that build the ontology and write each answer's SQL run on NVIDIA's hosted API catalog (integrate.api.nvidia.com); point the endpoints at self-hosted NIM to keep inference in house. Connect agents through the MCP query tools with uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp; each user signs in, and every call runs with that user's application permissions. Generated SQL runs with the connected database account's rights, so use a dedicated read-only account limited to the tables and views you intend to expose. Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin and the web app on the host, so replace every default password first, and keep ports 3001 and 3002 on a private network because the ingestion endpoints have no authentication of their own. Setting KUMO_RFM_API_KEY makes the agent upload connected tables to the hosted KumoRFM service for predictive questions. Apache-2.0.

resources.name: MiniCPM-OCR
resources.description: An open-weight OCR model family that parses Chinese and English PDFs and images into Markdown or JSON, with a second model that scores how reliable each recognised region is.
resources.for_whom: Teams building document agents or extraction pipelines who want OCR they can run on their own GPU, with a score that flags regions for human review.
resources.access_notes: Install the SDK with python -m pip install --upgrade "minicpm-ocr[all]" (Python 3.10 or later) plus the PaddlePaddle GPU packages for layout detection, then serve the recognition model with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama or FlagOS. The tutorial's vLLM route needs Linux x86_64, an NVIDIA GPU with driver 580 or later and at least 40 GB of disk, and it builds vLLM from source; the Docker image needs Linux x86-64, an NVIDIA GPU, a CUDA 12.9 compatible driver and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. Deployed locally, document processing and inference stay on your machine, and the tutorial starts vLLM on 127.0.0.1; the first install and model downloads need internet. The free hosted API and online demo run at platform.modelbest.ai, so documents sent there leave your machine. The README suggests telling a coding agent to "Read and execute" a remote SKILL.md that sets up environments and downloads models: read it yourself before handing it over. Apache-2.0, covering code and model weights.

resources.name: OpenWorker
resources.description: An open-source desktop AI coworker that runs on your computer, works across your files, terminal and more than 25 connected apps such as GitHub, Slack and Gmail, and asks for approval before writes, sends and shell commands.

Running from source needs Python 3.10 or later, Node 20 or later and the Rust toolchain. Conversations, connector tokens and model keys stay in the app's local secret store, and data leaves only through the model and connectors you choose. The one cloud piece brokers OAuth sign-ins for connectors; it is used with an optional free account for one-click connections such as Slack, and everything works signed out with your own keys. Actions are approval-gated by default; an optional auto-approve mode lets a reviewer model pass routine actions, and commands can run in an NVIDIA OpenShell container, the macOS sandbox or a hidden Windows account. The app is in open beta and updates itself. The app is free and you pay your model provider directly. MIT.

resources.name: Cactus
resources.description: A Python package that runs small text, speech and vision models locally, with tool calling, structured extraction, transcription, image description and fine-tuning.
resources.for_whom: Developers who want an agent to call tools, extract structured data or transcribe speech on a laptop or consumer device, with inference running locally.
resources.access_notes: Install with pip install -U cactus-compute; it needs Python 3.9 or later. On first use it downloads and caches the engine and the requested model weights from Hugging Face, then inference runs locally. agent.run() executes your Python functions as soon as the model picks them; use complete() to inspect proposed calls before running them. The package sends anonymous usage counts (function name, package version, OS and a random install ID, which the docs say never include prompts, outputs or data). The README says CACTUS_TELEMETRY=0 turns this off, and the repo's llms.txt names NEEDLE_TELEMETRY=0 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Fine-tuning needs pip install "cactus-compute[train]", and the documented synthetic data step is set up with an OPENROUTER_API_KEY. The hosted Cactus Platform for fine-tuning needs a CACTUS_API_KEY, and each finetune or generate job spends account allowance at submission. The Needle 3, Whistle and Mirage weights are tagged apache-2.0 on Hugging Face. Apache-2.0.

resources.description: A self-hosted kanban board and MCP server in one program, where coding agents take tasks, move cards and comment on the same board you use in the browser.
resources.for_whom: Developers running Claude Code, Codex or another MCP client who want one task board shared between themselves and their agents.

The easiest path is to deploy a model on Microsoft Foundry and point fara-cli at its endpoint URL and API key, with no GPU or model download; otherwise download the weights from Hugging Face and serve them with vLLM on your own GPUs, with a context length of at least 15000 tokens. Each step gives the model a screenshot of the browser and the conversation history, so those go to whichever endpoint hosts it, and runs save per-step screenshots and a data_point.json to the output folder. Microsoft calls it a research preview and recommends running it in a sandbox, monitoring it, and avoiding sensitive data and high-risk sites; Magentic-UI adds a sandboxed browser with action logs and prompts at critical points. MIT for the code and the model weights.

resources.name: BLA (Blind LLM Agents)
resources.description: A Node.js CLI, MCP server and agent skill that alters the software you ship so AI reverse-engineering agents hit resource limits and follow decoys, while runtime behaviour is meant to stay the same.
resources.for_whom: Developers who ship binaries, Electron apps, JavaScript bundles, Python or WebAssembly and want automated AI reverse engineering of their own releases to cost more.
resources.access_notes: Run npx bla-agents setup to register the bla MCP server and blind-llm-agents skill with your coding agents, then npx bla-agents harden . to audit, protect and verify build outputs; it needs Node.js ^22.23.4 or >=24.0.0. Setup auto-discovers installed coding agents and writes to their global config files, such as ~/.claude.json and ~/.cursor/mcp.json; use --client to limit it and npx bla-agents uninstall to remove it. Protection adds decoy metadata, honey tables and canary credentials to your artifacts and can make them much larger (the README lists an Electron ASAR going from 607 B to 16.9 MiB), and it adds inspector and Frida detection that returns synthetic telemetry, so run bla verify against the original in staging before shipping. Risky LLM-facing bait, including fake COPPA or medical notices, is off unless you pass --llm-directives. The MCP tools refuse to overwrite an existing output file unless confirm_overwrite: true is set. The README's token and cost multipliers are the project's own internal estimates. Only run it on software you own or are authorised to modify. The npm package is published from this repo with npm provenance. MIT.

resources.name: Ansvisor

resources.access_notes: Self-host: clone the repo, copy the web and server .env example files, run the migration SQL in a Supabase project (the free tier works), then install the web app with Yarn and the server with npm, or run docker compose up --build. Needs Node.js 20 or later, a key for at least one AI provider (OpenAI, Google Gemini or Anthropic) and a Cloro key for collecting answers from AI platforms; Site Audit also needs Scrape.do, and DataForSEO, Tavily, OpenRouter and Composio are optional. Connect Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP client to /api/mcp with an ans_ API key sent as a bearer header; app.ansvisor.com/api/mcp is the hosted endpoint on Ansvisor's servers. Docker Compose publishes the web app on port 3000 and the API on port 80, and the first user to sign up becomes the admin, so register first and put a firewall in front. Send to CMS sends WordPress pages as drafts for you to publish. Agents that publish on their own are off by default and need server flags, an Admin switch and per-agent permission.
